dob_8inch.name: SS Cyg
dob_8inch.notes: chart X42882PV — Dwarf nova, monitor for outburst

dob_8inch.name: M57
dob_8inch.notes: Ring nebula.  Looks like smoke ring.

dob_8inch.name: M1
dob_8inch.notes: Crab nebula. Remnant of a supernova in the year 1054.

dob_8inch.name: M73
dob_8inch.notes: Very difficult, small grouping of stars

dob_8inch.name: M44
dob_8inch.notes: Beehive cluster.  358 stars approx. 500 ly distant

dwarf_mini.name: Veil Nebula (Western)
dwarf_mini.notes: Supernova remnant. Eastern half is NGC 6992.

dwarf_mini.name: Veil Nebula (Eastern)
dwarf_mini.notes: Brighter arc of the Veil. Pairs with NGC 6960.

dwarf_mini.name: Pleiades
dwarf_mini.notes: THE wide-field target. Reflection nebulosity around stars.

dwarf_mini.name: Coat Hanger (Brocchi's Cluster)
dwarf_mini.notes: Asterism, not true cluster. Perfect wide-field shape.

dwarf_mini.name: California Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Very wide, low surface brightness. Needs long exposure.

dwarf_mini.name: North America Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Huge, continent-shaped. Ideal for wide field.

dwarf_mini.name: Perseus Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: ~100 stars. Autumn target.

dwarf_mini.name: Cygnus Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Large, loose. Summer target near Deneb.

dwarf_mini.name: Elephant's Trunk Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Enormous faint nebula in Cepheus. Needs dark sky.

dwarf_mini.name: Starfish Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Auriga trio member. Cross-shaped.

dwarf_mini.name: Pinwheel Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Auriga trio member.

dwarf_mini.name: Double Cluster (h Persei)
dwarf_mini.notes: Pairs with NGC 884. Spectacular in wide field.

dwarf_mini.name: Double Cluster (chi Persei)
dwarf_mini.notes: Companion to NGC 869, same FOV.

dwarf_mini.name: Aquarius Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Dense, slightly oval. Autumn target.

dwarf_mini.name: Pacman Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Cassiopeia, pacman shape. Autumn target.

dwarf_mini.name: Auriga Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Richest of the Auriga trio. ~500 stars.

dwarf_mini.name: Owl Cluster (ET Cluster)
dwarf_mini.notes: Cassiopeia. Two bright "eyes" + body shape.

dwarf_mini.name: Stock 2
dwarf_mini.notes: Near Double Cluster. Large, loose.

dwarf_mini.name: Ophiuchus Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Large, loose. Low surface brightness — needs wide field.

dwarf_mini.name: Gemini Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Rich. Small cluster NGC 2158 nearby in FOV.

dwarf_mini.name: Great Hercules Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Best northern globular. Summer target.

dwarf_mini.name: Eagle Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Pillars of Creation. Includes cluster NGC 6611.

dwarf_mini.name: Omega/Swan Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Bright, distinctive swan shape.

dwarf_mini.name: Orion Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Brightest nebula. Pairs with M43. Winter target.

dwarf_mini.name: Cone Nebula / Christmas Tree
dwarf_mini.notes: Includes Christmas Tree open cluster.

dwarf_mini.name: Rosette Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Open cluster at center of Rosette Nebula.

dwarf_mini.name: De Mairan's Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Companion to M42, same FOV.

dwarf_mini.name: Sagittarius Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: One of best globulars. Large and bright.

dwarf_mini.name: Rosette Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Pairs with open cluster NGC 2244 in center.

dwarf_mini.name: Trifid Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Pairs with M8 Lagoon. Emission + reflection.

dwarf_mini.name: Lagoon Nebula
dwarf_mini.notes: Large, pairs with M20 Trifid in same wide FOV.

dwarf_mini.name: Serpens Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Among finest globulars. Spring/summer.

dwarf_mini.name: Beehive Cluster (Praesepe)
dwarf_mini.notes: Large, bright. Best in small scopes / binoculars.

dwarf_mini.name: Canis Major Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Bright, easy. Below Sirius.

dwarf_mini.name: Puppis Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Bright, pairs with M46 in same wide FOV.

dwarf_mini.name: Puppis Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Contains planetary NGC 2438 in foreground.

dwarf_mini.name: Hydra Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: Large, triangular shape.

dwarf_mini.name: Cancer Cluster
dwarf_mini.notes: One of oldest known clusters. ~4 billion years.
